title: MetLife Building
visualBrief: The broad octagonal 200 Park Avenue tower, with projecting quartz-aggregate precast window fins, two deeply recessed mechanical floors, roof lettering, aluminum-clad eighth/ninth floors and the renewed travertine north arcade.

nativeAxes.origin: Original mapped whole-building frame at reconstructed street grade

sourceFacts.architects: Emery Roth & Sons; Walter Gropius and Pietro Belluschi consulting
sourceFacts.facade: Eggshell precast concrete with exposed quartz aggregate; floor-to-floor tower units and separate base spandrels/mullions
sourceFacts.facadePrimaryEvidence: Architectural Forum, February 1962, printed page 10: Concrete Curtain; present facade restoration by Hoffmann Architects
sourceFacts.renewedNorthEntry: MdeAS 2022 renovation: travertine arcade columns, bronze frames and large glazing
sourceFacts.terrace: Current owner brochure describes an eighth-floor open-air Skyline Terrace and Lounge

reconstruction.plan: Independent mapped twelve-point tower ring is cleaned only at near-collinear vertices to retain its long octagonal shape. The much wider full ground podium, setback eighth/ninth-floor block and four separate support columns retain their own footprints.
reconstruction.facade: Continuous inset blue-grey glazing is divided by merged precast spandrels and vertical piers. Continuous triangular fins preserve the cast projection without per-floor end caps. Fine seal gaps/transoms are omitted; two mechanical levels have real setback glazing and outer columns.
reconstruction.crown: Physical vertical fins stand before a recessed louver screen; original white polygonal MetLife lettering faces the broad north/south walls. Flat roof and modest cornice retain the architectural height; no active helipad is depicted.
reconstruction.entry: Current north-side colonnade is recessed behind travertine-clad piers, with bronze-framed tall glazing, three revolving doors and soffit lights. The separate podium terrace has glass guards and simple planter beds.

reviewStatus: source-geometry; near/far and shared-material captures pending
limitations: Original437075triangles/52320792byte per-cell detailed master remains exactly reproducible through unchanged buildMetlife recipe. Reviewed source merges repeating precast spandrels, vertical piers and triangular fins around continuous inset glazing instead of independent framed window boxes. It retains all original major facade floor datums, two genuinely recessed mechanical levels, separate support-column footprints, crown screen/fins and original polygonal north/south lettering, north arcade/soffit, three revolving doors and podium terrace. Fine cell seam gaps/transoms and per-cell glass tint variation are removed; all original detail remains available through unchanged master recipe. Skyline aggregates facade ribbons/piers and uses flat original letter faces, coarse arcade/door rings and shared graph colour means. District restores sampled vertical piers and dark recesses; street restores each facade datum/pier, continuous0.33m triangular shaft fins and extruded signage while flattening spandrel/pier return faces; close-up retains continuous triangular fins and finer entry/terrace grids. Concrete, travertine and coated-metal canonical graphs supply four near draw groups including one opaque glass group; no embedded images. Original door transparency becomes tinted opaque panels; no interior transparency/fit-out claim. Exact panel pitch, recess elevations, fin dimensions, signage outline and entrance/terrace details remain photo reconstructions. No surveyed grade or physical-device performance claim. Skyline omits revolving-door hardware, tiny fixtures and the outer mechanical-recess columns, retaining the inset dark belts and their floor/ceiling caps; only one pair of spandrels is sampled per shaft zone. Skyline arcade columns use a coarser spacing. Street strips use flat front faces; their triangular cast fins still have three actual side faces and both end caps. Far glazing sits2cm behind the facade strips instead of24.5cm, preventing coplanar overlap while approximating the facade depth. Per-level errors describe finite tested broad surfaces, excluding omitted slender columns/fins and entrance hardware, not a global Hausdorff bound.
importReason: Preserve thin facade frames, panel joints and crown/antenna details until a measured LOD chain is authored.
